s1

This short video shows how to turn a messy data folder into a clean dataset that others can find, trust, and cite. We use three tools from our fair data curation repo. Think of it like getting a passport: you give your facts once, and every checkpoint reads the same page.
s2

There are four steps. One: the FAIR Folder Curator scans your folder and reads dates, GPS, and sensors from the files. Two: the Study Card Builder collects everything else, once. Three: the Curator uses that study card to plan a clean layout and writes a script. Four: you check the result with make manifest, then deposit it to get a DOI.
s3

Step one. Open the FAIR Folder Curator in Chrome or Edge, and drop in your folder. Nothing is uploaded. It reads only file names, sizes, dates, and headers. Here is a messy maize drone folder: three hundred thirteen files, seventeen point seven gigabytes, three junk files, and two possible duplicates.
s4

Scroll down to Metadata inside the files. The Curator pulls capture dates, the GPS center, and sensor models out of the image, LiDAR, and hyperspectral headers. Save the session. It becomes the starting point for the next app.
s5

Step two. Open the Study Card Builder and press Import from Curator session. Dates, location, and sensors are filled in for you. Then pick your dataset type. There are seventeen, grouped into field, lab, sensors, and models. Each one changes the questions and the folder layout.
s6

In Sensors and settings, press Add suggested sensors. Fill in the model, serial number, and the settings you used. Red On the day tags mark facts you must write down while you collect. Nothing can recover them later.
s7

Next, write the collection protocol as short numbered steps, so a new student could repeat it without asking you. Then list every column of your results table, with its unit, an ontology ID, and whether the value was observed, derived, or simulated.
s8

On Review and download, one zip gives you everything: the study card, README, data dictionary, sensors, protocol, MIAPPE, Croissant, and ready-made files for Hugging Face, Zenodo, Kaggle, and Ag Data Commons. Save your progress file too.
s9

Step three. Go back to the Curator and press Load study card. The interview now shows only what is still missing. README, MIAPPE, and Croissant are switched off here, because the builder already wrote them. One source of truth.

Check the planned layout, then export the kit. Run organize dot py once to preview. Nothing changes. Run it again with dash dash apply to copy files into the new layout. Your originals stay where they are, and every run can be undone.

Step four. Run make manifest dot py on the organized folder. It writes checksums and a quality report that lists junk files, duplicates, empty files, and names that break your ID rule. Fix them and run it again.

Then deposit the folder in a repository, get a DOI, enter it in the builder so every file carries it, and tick the finish checklist. In one line: describe it once, organize it with the Curator, check it, and deposit it.
